key_insight: A soft robotic hand exoskeleton can help people with severe hand impairment regain intentional grasping for everyday tasks. By adding wrist dorsiflexion support and an active opposable thumb, the device restores more natural, dexterous hand movements.
problem_solved: People with severe hand paralysis often cannot perform functional grasps needed for daily activities like feeding. This paper addresses the lack of practical, lightweight assistive devices that can restore meaningful hand function.
method: Designed a lightweight textile glove-based soft hand exoskeleton for wearability and comfort.
Added wrist dorsiflexion assistance to improve hand positioning and grasp initiation.
Integrated an active opposable thumb to increase hand articulation and enable more dexterous grasp types.
impact: For AI/ML and robotics practitioners, this shows how soft robotic assistive systems can translate control and design advances into real functional gains for humans. It highlights the value of human-centered, dexterous actuation in rehabilitation robotics and assistive technology.
visual_elements: Before/after illustration of a user with severe hand impairment performing a grasping task

paper_title: A dexterous soft hand exoskeleton restores intentional grasping in individuals with severe hand impairment
paper_authors: John Nassour, Nicolas Berberich, Daniel Utpadel-Fischler, Tobias Wächter, Gordon Cheng
